transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been going on that made you decide to come see me?

Well, doctor, it’s... it’s a whole situation at work, and honestly, it’s been building up for a while now. I’m a transportation inspector, and I take my job very seriously, you know? Making sure everything is up to code, doing things by the book. And a little while back, I actually won this county safety award. It was a nice recognition, or so I thought at the time. But ever since they handed me that award, things have just... shifted. It's like it put a massive target on my back. 

Certain people at work—people I thought I had a decent working relationship with—have been actively going through my old files and twisting my inspection reports. They’ll take a perfectly standard sign-off and try to make it look like I cut corners or missed something. And it’s not just the reports, it’s the finances too. Out of nowhere, they keep asking these really pointed budget questions, digging into my mileage and equipment logs, wording things in this very specific way like they’re trying to make me look crooked. Like I'm skimming from the county or taking bribes or something! 

I even brought all this to my supervisor, thinking he'd step in and put a stop to it, but he just waved me off. He gave me this whole speech about how it’s "just a normal review process" and I shouldn't take it personally. But I've been doing this job since I got out of high school. I know what a normal review looks like, and this isn't it. The way they CC upper management on minor emails, the timing of these questions... I can just tell, without a shadow of a doubt, that there is a coordinated effort to discredit me and ruin my reputation. It’s a full-on campaign to push me out, and it’s just... well, that's why I'm here. Because nobody at the depot is listening to the facts.

When you say people are coordinating against you, what is the most concrete piece of evidence that convinces you this is definitely happening—something you could show me or describe in specific detail?

Well, if you want concrete, I can give you concrete, because I've actually started keeping copies of everything in a separate folder at home just to keep track of it all. Take last Wednesday, for example. Or no, wait, it was Thursday, because Wednesday it rained and I was stuck doing depot paperwork. Thursday morning, I submit a report on the Route 9 overpass drainage grates. I’ve been inspecting those exact same grates since, what, 2015? I know every single rust spot on them. I marked the report "satisfactory with routine monitoring." That is standard county code. It’s by the book. It’s exactly what you write when a structure is perfectly safe but aging. 

But then, less than twenty-four hours later, I get this email from the compliance office. And they didn't just email me, doctor, they CC'd the regional director. The regional director! Over a drainage grate! And the email asks me to clarify if my assessment of "routine monitoring" indicates a potential structural liability that I wasn't fully documenting. Do you see what they're doing there? They are taking my standard inspection reports and twisting them to make it look on paper like I'm cutting corners or hiding liabilities. 

And it doesn't stop with the reports. It bleeds over into the finances, which makes zero sense because I don't even handle the department budget! But suddenly, I’m getting these incredibly pointed budget questions about my daily mileage and equipment logs. Last week, they sent me a formal request to justify a fourteen-mile discrepancy on my truck's odometer. Fourteen miles! I drive all over this county every single day. But they worded the email in this very specific, legal-sounding way, saying they needed to "ensure all fuel expenditures align strictly with approved, non-commercial routes." They are trying to make me look crooked. They're trying to build this fake paper trail to make it look like I'm skimming county gas money or driving out to take bribes from private contractors or something insane like that. 

I literally printed these emails out. I took them to my supervisor, laid them right on his desk, and said, "Look at this. Look at the wording. Look at who they are CCing." And he barely even glanced at the pages. He just gave me this patronizing little sigh and told me it’s just a normal review process, that the county is tightening its belt, and I need to let it go. A normal review! I've been doing this job since I was eighteen years old. I know the protocol inside and out. Interrogating an inspector over fourteen miles is not normal. 

It all goes back to that county safety award. Before I got that award, nobody looked twice at my odometer. But ever since they handed me that plaque, it's like a switch flipped. I can just tell—I mean, it is clear as day if you actually look at the documents—there is a coordinated effort to discredit me. They want to ruin my reputation and push me out, and they're using these twisted reports and budget questions to do it.

Outside of work—with your family, friends, or in other areas of your life—do you feel like people are working against you or plotting in other ways, or is this concern really just focused on what's happening at your job?

Well, no, doctor, it's really... it's just the job. I mean, my life outside of work is, you know, it's pretty normal. I'm not... I'm not paranoid, if that's what you're getting at. I know how this sounds, I really do, but it's contained to the depot. 

Like, take my mornings, for instance. I'm up at 5:30 AM, every single day, just like I have been for the last ten years. I make my coffee—black, no sugar, because I'm trying to watch my weight, you know how it is when you're sitting in a county truck all day—and I'm out the door by 6:15. I get to work on time, I do my pre-inspection checks on the vehicle, I get my route assignment, and I go out and do my job. I complete every single inspection, by the book, just like I always have. I haven't missed a day of work through all of this. I'm still doing my job, and I'm doing it well. 

And outside of that, you know, I still go to church on Sundays. I go to First Presbyterian over on Elm Street. I've been going there since I was a kid. I still help out with the food drive every Thanksgiving, I still talk to the same people after the service. Nobody there is acting weird or, you know, out to get me. My family is fine, my friends are fine. We still get together for a barbecue now and then, watch the game, whatever. I take care of myself. I keep my house clean, I pay my bills on time, I take my truck in for its oil changes right on schedule. My life is completely normal. 

The only time—the *only* time—things get bad, the only time there's a problem, is when I'm at work and somebody brings up one of those twisted reports, or they start questioning my spending or my mileage. That's when the whole thing flares up, because that's where the problem actually is. It's not in my head, doctor, it's in those emails. It's in the way they look at me in the breakroom when they think I'm not paying attention. It's confined entirely to the people who are threatened by that safety award and want me gone. So, no, it's not my family or my friends. It's just... it's just them. At work.

When your supervisor told you this was just a normal review process, was there any part of you that wondered if he might actually be right, or are you completely certain he's mistaken and that this is definitely a coordinated campaign against you?

I mean, I really tried to sit with what he said, I really did. I walked out of his office that day, I went straight out to the lot, got into my truck, and I just sat there staring at the steering wheel for a good twenty minutes. I played devil's advocate with myself. I asked myself, you know, am I overreacting? Is this just how things are now? 

But doctor, you have to understand the reality of the situation. I am completely, one hundred percent certain that he is mistaken. I have zero doubts. Because I'm sitting here talking to you today specifically because of what is actually happening. Ever since I got that county safety award—which, by the way, was supposed to be a proud moment, something you put on your mantle, right?—ever since that exact moment, certain people at work have been relentlessly twisting my inspection reports. 

A normal review process does not involve taking a standard, by-the-book sign-off and trying to spin it into some massive structural liability that I supposedly ignored. And it definitely doesn't involve these sudden, incredibly pointed budget questions out of nowhere. I mean, interrogating me over fourteen miles on my odometer? Wording their emails with all this legal jargon like they’re trying to make me look crooked? Like I'm stealing from the county? That is not normal administrative oversight. 

So even when my supervisor sits there, barely even glancing at the printed emails I brought him, and gives me this whole speech about how it’s just a normal review and the county is tightening its belt... I know he's wrong. He's either completely blind to office politics, or he just doesn't want the headache of dealing with it. But I can tell. I read those emails, I see who they are copying on them, and I can tell you as a matter of absolute fact that there is a coordinated effort to discredit me. They are building a fake paper trail to ruin my reputation, and my supervisor brushing it off doesn't change the facts of what they're doing. It just means I'm on my own in dealing with it.

When you look back at those emails—the one about the drainage grates, the one about the fourteen miles—is there any possibility at all that they could have been sent for routine administrative reasons, or are you absolutely certain there is no other explanation besides a coordinated campaign against you?

Look, doctor, I understand why you have to ask that, I really do. It is your job to look for the simple answer, right? To see if maybe I am just misinterpreting things. But no. No, there is absolutely zero possibility that this is just routine administrative whatever. Zero. Because you have to look at the whole picture, the whole timeline of how this all started. 

I am here talking to you today because ever since I got that county safety award, the whole atmosphere changed. Before that award, I was just a guy doing his job, getting the inspections done, flying under the radar. But ever since they handed me that, certain people at work have been relentlessly twisting my inspection reports. If it was routine, they would just file the report and move on, like they have for years. But they are taking my standard sign-offs and twisting them to look like liabilities, and then on top of that, they are asking these incredibly pointed budget questions. Out of nowhere! Asking about my mileage and my equipment logs in this way that is clearly designed to make me look crooked. Like I am skimming money or doing something illegal out on the routes. That does not happen in a routine review. 

And I know I told you about my supervisor, and I know he sat there and told me to my face that it is just a normal review process. But even when my supervisor says it is just a normal review, it doesn't change what is actually on the page. I can tell. I read between the lines, I see who is getting copied on these emails, I see the timing of it all right after the award. There is a coordinated effort to discredit me. I am absolutely certain of it. There is just no other logical explanation for why they would suddenly be building this massive, fake paper trail against a guy who has done nothing but good work for them. It is a coordinated effort to push me out, doctor, plain and simple, and there is no routine administrative reason that explains it. None.

But even when my supervisor says it is just a normal review, it doesn't change what is actually on the page. I can tell. I read between the lines, I see who is getting copied on these emails, I see the timing of it all right after the award. There is a coordinated effort to discredit me. I am absolutely certain of it. There is just no other logical explanation for why they would suddenly be building this massive, fake paper trail against a guy who has done nothing but good work for them. It is a coordinated effort to push me out, doctor, plain and simple, and there is no routine administrative reason that explains it. None.

inference.note: Patient demonstrates fixed, false beliefs (delusions) about coordinated persecution at work that persist despite contradictory evidence from supervisor and reasonable alternative explanations. Key features support Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type (F22.0) rather than Unspecified Delusional Disorder (F22.9): (1) Non-bizarre delusions focused on being conspired against; (2) Functioning remains intact outside the delusional system (work performance, family, church, daily routine all normal); (3) Clear temporal onset tied to specific event (safety award); (4) Patient maintains absolute certainty despite supervisor's reassurance and logical alternatives; (5) Absence of hallucinations or other psychotic features mentioned. The specificity of the persecutory theme and preserved functioning outside this domain strongly favors the more specific F22.0 code.
